clue.text: More annoyed about overture from naked disruptive partner in bed

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: sorer means more annoyed, as in sore at someone

indicators.note: an overture is the opening of a piece, so this takes the first letter of naked

explanation.surface: Someone grows crosser at their bedfellow, who sleeps naked and keeps them awake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N (the opening of 'naked') inside SORER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who snores noisily keeps the person sharing the bed awake, a disruptive bedfellow.

clue.text: Offer to limit crook's second time in prison

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so the bid surrounds the letter

parts.note: a bid is an offer at auction

indicators.note: second picks out the second letter of crook

explanation.surface: A crook is offered a deal to cut down a second prison stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to limit' puts R, the second letter of 'crook', inside BID.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing bird is British slang for serving a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time.

clue.text: Academic in pursuit of quality accepting nothing, allowing no leaks

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following, so the academic comes after the quality

parts.note: water means quality, as in a gem of the first water

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the academic holds the zero

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A scholar chasing excellence admits nothing, giving nothing away to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quality' comes from the jeweller's grading of gems, 'of the first water'. 'accepting' and 'in pursuit of' signal the insertion and the order; 'leaks' suggests secrets, not water.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impervious to water lets no liquid seep through, so it allows no leaks.

clue.text: Very old suggestion each dismissed as ineffectual

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: an idea is a suggestion put forward

explanation.surface: An ancient proposal is rejected point by point as useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' removes EA from IDEA, leaving ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract that is null and without legal force is ineffectual.

clue.text: Soiling our rocks? Not marvellous

indicators.note: rocks means shakes up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting our stones dirty is hardly a glorious achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' scrambles SOILINGOUR. The definition plays on the answer as un-glorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameful and lacking honour or fame, hence the opposite of wonderful.

clue.text: Loosen United? New soccer group's trimmed soccer team

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
the FA is the Football Association, England's governing body, plus the S of the possessive
a soccer team has eleven players, so one trimmed off leaves ten

explanation.surface: A football club wonders about a new league having its squad cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is the Football Association, which runs English football. A team of eleven trimmed by one gives TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a fastening, such as a buckle or button, is to loosen it.

clue.text: Articles about alcohol leading to chest pain

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the drink

parts.note: AN and A are both indefinite articles
gin is a spirit, alcohol

explanation.surface: Pieces of writing on drinking claim it brings on heart trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' means two of them here, one either side; 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical condition is pain in the chest caused by poor blood supply to the heart.

clue.text: Most prominent councillor conceding

parts.note: owning, as in owning up, means conceding or admitting

explanation.surface: A senior local councillor admits defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The crowning achievement is the supreme, topmost one, the highest point.

clue.text: Declare sketch to be rubbish? Get rid of the rubbish!

indicators.note: rubbish here describes the letters as junk to be sorted again, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic pans a comedy sketch, then demands the waste be cleared away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rubbish' scrambles DECLARESKETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from sailors clearing a ship before battle, means removing clutter to get ready for action.

clue.text: Game had to involve one of its players in an advanced position

parts.note: bridge is a card game

indicators.note: to involve means to include within, so the player sits inside had

parts.note: taken as written
bridge is played by North, South, East and West, so E for East is a player

explanation.surface: A card game includes one of its participants at a forward seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The four players at a bridge table are named North, South, East and West. 'to involve' puts E inside HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A military foothold seized in enemy territory, from which to push forward, is an advanced position.

clue.text: Idle youngster on farm having bounds reset?

indicators.note: the bounds are the outer letters, reset meaning put in a new place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a foal is a young horse, seen on farms

explanation.surface: A young farm animal is idle when its fences are moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having bounds reset' swaps the end letters of FOAL, F and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge about doing nothing is to be idle; loaf is the verb.

clue.text: Cliff desiring no French wine

indicators.note: no means without, so those letters are removed

parts.note: craving means desiring
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: Someone on a cliff wants nothing to do with French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes VIN from CRAVING.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep, rugged rock face is a cliff.

clue.text: Worker with time to burn limited by great work schedule

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in on both sides, so the great letters enclose the rest

parts.note: GT is the abbreviation for great
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker
to char is to burn

explanation.surface: A labourer with hours to waste is held back by a huge project timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited by' means the abbreviation for great sits at both ends, split around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar chart named after Henry Gantt that plots project tasks against time, a project schedule.

clue.text: Do chatter about Queen and corgi, say

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the chatter goes around the others

parts.note: to prate is to chatter
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a corgi is an example of a pet, say marking the example

explanation.surface: Gossip about the Queen and her famous corgis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the wrap. 'Do' is a verb here, as in carrying out a crime, not a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit a crime or misdeed is to do it.

clue.text: Brought about sex in valley, after going for a climb

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the valley word is written backwards

parts.note: a dene is a narrow wooded valley
gender means sex

explanation.surface: A couple go hiking and end up making love in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after going for a climb' turns the valley word upward to read ENED; 'in' places the sex word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cause or give rise to something is to bring it about.

clue.text: Absolutely representing impact of terroir?

definitions.meaning: terroir is soil, so something hitting the soil has come all the way to earth

explanation.surface: A wine buff asks how the soil shows through in a vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: Terroir is the wine term for the soil and site of a vineyard; taking the phrase literally, a fall ends there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely or thoroughly, as in suiting someone perfectly.

clue.text: Company backed opera tunes after receipt of new instruments

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards, so the company letters are reversed
receipt means taking in, so the tunes enclose the new letter

parts.note: arias are solo songs in opera

explanation.surface: A firm supports opera music after taking delivery of fresh equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reads like sponsorship but signals the reversal; 'after receipt of' both orders the pieces and puts the new letter inside the tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: These small egg-shaped wind instruments with finger holes are musical instruments.

clue.text: One's defeat laid out in American novel

indicators.note: laid out means spread and rearranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A personal defeat is set out in a work of American fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' scrambles ONESDEFEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck's 1952 novel, filmed with James Dean, is a classic of US fiction.

clue.text: Description of work a little curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a speck is a tiny bit, a little

explanation.surface: A job description is cut a bit short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the K at the end of SPECK.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for specification, a detailed statement of what a job must deliver.

clue.text: Group of stage performers rather promoting English play, ultimately

indicators.note: English is E, and in a down clue promoting it lifts it to the top, so the E moves to the front

parts.note: quite means rather, as in quite good

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of play

explanation.surface: Actors are fairly keen to put on an English drama in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting English' moves the E of QUITE to the front, giving EQUIT; 'ultimately' adds Y from 'play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the British actors' trade union, a body of stage performers.

clue.text: Surface not popular for marine creature

indicators.note: not means without, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a finish is a surface coating, as on furniture
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A seabed surface is unloved by sea life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes IN from FINISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A cod or mackerel swimming in the sea is a typical marine creature.

clue.text: Manœuvre to beat leading figures in horse-racing

parts.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre for position
to club is to beat

explanation.surface: Jostling to strike the front-runners in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jockey Club was long the governing body of British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: This historic body ran British racing, so its members are the sport's senior figures.

clue.text: Curse Judge in identification of error

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark a teacher uses to identify a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A judge swears on spotting a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A hex or spell bringing bad luck is a curse.

clue.text: One end of coloured string

wordplay.reading: C at the start, or else D at the finish

parts.note: coloured begins and ends with different consonants, and the phrase is read literally as offering either of them, with the linking word meaning alternatively

explanation.surface: A tip of a dyed thread.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay literally: one end of 'coloured' is C OR D.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin rope or twine is string.

clue.text: American taxmen backtracking, with criminal groups about — they put the heat on

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the gangs go round the taxmen

parts.note: gangs are groups of criminals

indicators.note: backtracking means going back, so the taxmen letters are reversed

parts.note: the IRS is the US Internal Revenue Service

explanation.surface: US tax officials retreat as mobsters close in, applying pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracking' signals the reversal and 'about' the wrap. 'put the heat on' sounds like pressure but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Burners on a cooker hob apply heat to the pans placed on them.

clue.text: Mistakes? Time to accept reduction in incidence

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the time encloses the rest

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: reduction means cutting it shorter, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a rate is an incidence, how often something happens

explanation.surface: Is it a mistake for the age to tolerate fewer cases?
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduction in' drops the last letter of the incidence word; 'to accept' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing errors added to a book; the Latin plural of erratum.
